verification_note: `|params| { body }` is a real closure literal, capturing free variables (like `base`) from its enclosing scope at the point it's created; calling it directly or via a variable it's been assigned to both work identically (add_to_base(5) and f(5), where f=add_to_base, both give 15); a closure-returning function (outer) produces genuinely INDEPENDENT closures per call, each with its own captured `n` (add10(1)=11, add20(1)=21 -- not both sharing the last call's n)
